decisions.statement: A path under a page name is written by the change judging the pages named.
Every other TypeScript path is written by the change judging the imports named.
Every other path is written by the change judging the file alone.
A page arrives with its `id` worked out here rather than at the landing.
A caller saying no `id` is taken to have said `auto`.
An `id` a caller states goes in rather than an `id` worked out here.
An `id` stating nothing is refused rather than written into the page.
That refusal names leaving `id` out and saying `auto`.
A body already stating an `id` keeps that `id` under `auto`.
A body already stating an `id` refuses an `id` handed in beside that body.
A path naming no page takes no `id`.
Nothing here reads a path for its kind.
No list of the kinds that are pages is kept here.
Whether a path is a page is read from the module reading a path for its kind.
An entry takes its `id` at the change writing the body rather than here.
A path under a page type name is written by the change writing a page type.
A path under a page property name is written by the change judging the keys carried.

definition: one body written at one path, through the change writing that kind of path
